title: J01A — Freeze core cryptographic requirements and the v1 suite
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Freeze the shared primitive suite and direct-slot construction used by the experimental witnessed-first release. J19 owns the additional distributed construction and exact-artifact gate. This work does not establish that Jury is safe for real secrets. No production provider adapter or cryptographic implementation may land in J01A.

## Why This Task Exists

Provider availability must not choose Jury's security properties by accident.
Freezing the required properties, nonclaims, alternatives, contexts, and failure
behavior first gives J01B and J19 one stable provider-neutral contract to prove.

## Outcome

`docs/security/jury-v1-suite.md` contains a reviewable property matrix,
alternative comparison, explicit post-quantum and compliance decisions, and one
exact provider-neutral primitive suite and direct-slot construction before any
provider is selected.

## Required Work

- define required classical confidentiality/authenticity, recipient-compromise
  history exposure, nonce-misuse, key-binding/commitment, and failure behavior;
- decide whether stored recipient slots must resist harvest-now/decrypt-later
  attacks and separately whether signatures need post-quantum authenticity;
- compare classical RFC 9180 HPKE, pure ML-KEM HPKE, and
  X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid HPKE using exact key/ciphertext sizes, performance,
  portability, provider maturity, vector quality, and draft churn;
- use the exact core `draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-04` plus PQ
  `draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05` bytes and hashes frozen in master-plan section 0.21
  as the post-quantum HPKE comparison baseline; do not substitute a newer
  draft or the stale core `-03` bibliography reference without a semantic
  delta review and complete vector and composition revalidation;
- pin one mutually compatible HPKE core specification/revision, KEM profile,
  mode, KDF, and AEAD; define the exact outer sender-authentication composition
  when the selected KEM has no `AuthEncap`/`AuthDecap`, with no inferred
  authentication or classical fallback;
- compare AES-256-GCM-SIV, one-key/one-seal RFC 8439
  ChaCha20-Poly1305, and the exact expired XChaCha Internet-Draft profile for
  storage; do not equate larger nonces with misuse resistance;
- compare strict Ed25519 with a publicly specified and analyzed hybrid-signature
  alternative if PQ authenticity is required;
- freeze exact KEM/HPKE mode, AEADs, KDFs and contexts, MAC algorithm, MAC tag
  length and key/context schedule, hash/signature rules, Argon2id profiles,
  device-factor combiner, randomness treatment, encodings, limits, and error
  behavior;
- freeze every shared/direct cryptographic preimage byte-for-byte, including its
  domain prefix, field order, type and length encoding, integer encoding, suite
  identifier, KDF labels and inputs, HPKE `info`, every AAD, signature/hash/MAC
  input, and direct-slot component encoding; J05 must consume these bytes
  verbatim and may not redefine them;
- use the J03-owned representation contract in every cryptographic preimage:
  `VaultId`, `PrincipalId`, and `ItemId` contribute their exact nonzero 32 native
  bytes, never a ULID or their public hexadecimal JSON text;
- freeze the separate J01A identifier-generation contract: independent OS-CSPRNG
  full-width generation, no derivation or caller choice during ordinary
  creation, finite all-zero retry behavior, typed value-free entropy/retry
  failure, state-owner collision handling, the global-`VaultId` uniqueness
  nonclaim, and no partial object or signed-state publication;
- state that FIPS-validated deployment is a V1 non-goal and never infer a FIPS
  deployment claim from use of FIPS 203 ML-KEM;
- require one authenticated suite at lineage genesis, no negotiation or
  fallback, and authenticated re-encryption into a new lineage for migration;
- specify revision-scoped direct capsules plus descriptor/body secrets with
  fresh random `RevisionSealId` values; J19 owns the witnessed construction and
  may not weaken these suite, context, downgrade, or key-lifetime requirements.

- freeze the secret inputs, required constant-time behavior, provider/platform caveats, and local or remote observation model for every secret-bearing operation, including KEM decapsulation and implicit rejection, AEAD authentication comparisons, signature generation, KDF handling, and wrapper control flow or memory access.

## Required Verification

- independently recompute every size, algorithm identifier, and canonical
  encoding entry from pinned normative primary specifications;
- for every security-property cell, reproduce its exact security notion,
  attacker model, assumptions, pinned public analysis or proof, and the
  Jury-specific composition argument; unsupported properties remain explicitly
  unproven and unclaimed;
- demonstrate that every claimed property follows from the complete suite and
  canonical preimages, and that one weaker slot or fallback defeats the claim;
- specify positive, negative, fault, migration, and cross-provider vectors that
  J01B, J19, and J25 must realize;
- review nonce/key reuse, malformed-key/ciphertext, entropy failure, KDF
  exhaustion, draft-version substitution, secret-dependent control flow, and
  timing/validity-oracle cases at the construction level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- the matrix has no “broadly sound” or unstated property cells: each is yes, no,
  conditional with assumptions, or not required with rationale;
- every yes or conditional property cell pins an applicable public analysis or
  proof by exact revision and content hash when mutable and states the exact
  security notion, attacker model, assumptions, and complete-suite composition
  argument; absent support is recorded as unproven and unclaimed;
- HNDL resistance and PQ authenticity are explicit independent decisions;
- one exact suite and every J01A-owned shared or direct construction, context,
  encoding, and limit are frozen or J01A remains open; J19-owned witnessed
  constructions remain out of scope and may not weaken the frozen invariants;
- the J01A artifact contains the complete byte-exact shared/direct cryptographic
  preimage corpus and vectors that J01B binds; J05 only embeds those bytes and
  any change reopens the direct gate;
- the selected HPKE core revision, KEM profile, mode, KDF, AEAD, and outer
  sender-authentication composition are jointly specified and mutually
  compatible;
- the suite freezes the exact MAC algorithm, tag length, key derivation, domain
  separation, canonical input, comparison, and failure behavior used by local
  audit, checkpoint, and receipt authentication;
- every cryptographic preimage uses the exact J03 32-byte native identifier
  encoding and rejects ULID, hexadecimal-text, or other identifier
  substitutions;
- identifier generation is independently OS-random, non-derived, unavailable to
  ordinary caller choice, bounded on zero and state-known collision retries, and
  fail-closed on entropy or retry exhaustion without partial publication; one
  J03 generator is shared by all native ID types and global `VaultId` uniqueness
  is explicitly not claimed;
- every secret-bearing operation has an explicit constant-time/side-channel
  requirement or a bounded nonclaim with an attacker-observation rationale;
- every RFC, FIPS, or draft dependency is named with exact status and revision;
- FIPS-validated deployment is explicitly out of scope;
- no algorithm negotiation, fallback, mixed active suites, or in-place suite
  mutation is permitted;
- no production provider dependency, adapter, or cryptographic implementation
  lands.

## Dependencies

none.

## Unblocks

J01B, J03, and J05.

## Live Tracker Dependencies

None.

Unblocks J01B: `jury-qv4.1.2`.
Unblocks J03: `jury-qv4.2.2`.
Unblocks J05: `jury-qv4.2.4`.

title: J01B — Select and prove the cryptographic provider set
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Prove the shared providers and direct construction used as inputs to J19. Provider evidence and automated conformance feed but do not replace J19 exact-artifact verification and binding and do not make Jury suitable for real secrets.

## Why This Task Exists

Algorithm names do not establish provider behavior. Pinning actual implementations, feature surfaces, vectors, and wrapper normalization before product code lands prevents silent fallback, accidental dependency expansion, and security claims that exceed reproducible evidence.

## Outcome

Select the smallest provider set that implements exactly the J01A shared primitive suite and direct construction and record reproducible wrapper, supply-chain, and conformance evidence.

## Required Work

- Pin source revisions, checksums, features, MSRV, licenses, unsafe-code posture, maintenance status, and advisories.
- Document fallible entropy, allocation, malformed-input, error, and zeroization behavior without inferring guarantees.
- Map every J01A side-channel requirement to provider source evidence: constant-time guarantees, implicit rejection, comparison APIs, secret-dependent branches or memory access, and compiler/target/hardware caveats.
- Keep raw providers behind thin typed wrappers and exclude unrelated features.
- Where measurement is meaningful, add targeted differential/statistical timing tests for decapsulation, authentication, comparison, and wrapper paths; never present a passing timing test as proof of constant-time behavior.
- Bind the exact J01A suite artifact revision and content hash, canonical shared/direct preimage corpus and vector hashes, provider revisions, and specification hashes in docs/security/jury-v0-direct-crypto-gate.toml. This is a drift-prevention manifest, not a security certificate.

## Required Tests

Run provider suites at pinned revisions; compare at least two independent implementations where viable; test positive and negative semantics, canonical encodings, limits, entropy failures, zeroization paths, unsupported suites, and fallback rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- every provider and wrapper claim has reproducible dated evidence;
- every J01A side-channel requirement maps to provider source evidence and a
  wrapper invariant; an unknown or violated requirement keeps J01B open;
- selected providers implement exactly one J01A direct suite with no runtime fallback;
- independent implementations agree on accepted outputs and rejection semantics, or differences are normalized and tested;
- the dependency tree excludes unrelated plugin, SSH, PEM, legacy, and hazmat surfaces;
- the minimal direct-crypto gate binds the exact J01A artifact revision and
  content hash, canonical shared/direct preimage corpus, provider revisions,
  specifications, and vectors;
- no provider dependency, adapter, or cryptographic implementation lands before the J01A/J01B direct gate is accepted, and no witnessed implementation lands before J19's additional exact-artifact gate;
- no certification or independent-review claim is made;
- J19 consumes the exact pinned provider behavior and vectors; no witnessed implementation may treat this direct gate as a substitute for J19 verification and binding.

## Dependencies

J01A. Unblocks J04 and J19A.

title: J15 — Deliver post-0.x read-only Jig compatibility and copy-on-write migration
description:
## Post-0.x Compatibility Scope

This task is explicitly deferred and out of scope for the witnessed-access 0.x release. It has no parent-child relationship to the active release epic, is excluded from active readiness and estimates, and does not block J17, J25, J26, or any active release outcome. An operator may reactivate it only after J26 under a separately approved post-0.x compatibility scope.

## Why This Task Exists

Legacy migration can corrupt the only source copy or reproduce the security boundary Jury is replacing. A read-only, copy-on-write import into a fresh lineage makes every attempt reversible and independently verifiable while leaving retained legacy exposure explicit.

## Outcome

Valid legacy Jig v1/v2 vaults can be read through isolated compatibility types and copied into an absent Jury home without mutating or dual-writing the source.

## Required Work

- Accept bounded legacy inputs only through isolated read-only compatibility types; never write a legacy format.
- Require explicit source and absent, non-aliased destination.
- Create fresh Jury identifiers, keys, genesis, audit, checkpoint, and migration attestation.
- Verify legacy audit and bind the preserved archive digest.
- Prove source artifact and audit hashes remain unchanged across success and every injected failure.
- Keep identities and local rollback state outside repository destinations.
- Perform no implicit Git operation and retain explicit warnings about old full-access copies.

## Dependencies

J03, J05, J06, J07, J09, and J10. This task has no active 0.x dependents.

## Legacy Baseline and Provenance

Use https://github.com/bpcakes/jig-sh.git at exact commit eed70cee337b0067ed92deb9fa05017b0b284605; a sibling ../jig-sh is only an object source after the commit and every selected path verifies. If the exact object or a named path is unavailable, this task blocks rather than substituting another revision, build output, or the preserved source-plan snapshot.

Inspect as read-only compatibility input:

- crates/jig-vault/src/format.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/crypto.rs and aad.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault/envelope.rs and the minimum v1/v2 decode path;
- crates/jig-vault/src/audit.rs and store.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/legacy.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/tests/fixtures/** when present.

Reuse only proven decoders, validation limits, audit verification, fixtures, and failure cases. Replace the writer, in-place migration, v2 audit append, vault-ID preservation, global unlock, and home mutation with an isolated reader and absent Jury target.
notes: Jury owns the importer and absent destination. Jig-owned linking and rollback are tracked separately by D06 in the jig-sh repository. J15 is deferred and excluded from current release readiness; reactivation requires an explicit post-J26 compatibility scope.

title: J06 — Implement signed policy replay and exact access evaluation
description:
## Why This Task Exists

Authorization must come from one replayable signed history rather than current configuration, private catalog contents, or caller interpretation. A deterministic normalized state makes ownership, direct access, both witnessed quorums, and every downgrade independently auditable and deny-by-default.

## Outcome

Replay public signed policy from genesis into one deterministic normalized state that governs direct authority and witnessed membership, approval, quorum, workload, and downgrade rules without decrypting private item names.

## Required Design Contract

- Model vault principals, approvers, and witnesses as distinct subject classes. Only human vault principals may own; at least one human owner always remains.
- Model direct reader/writer roles separately from approver eligibility and witness membership.
- For every governed item, bind access mode, eligible approvers, eligible witnesses, approval quorum, witness quorum, allowed operations, maximum request lifetime, and workload constraints.
- Quorums count distinct active identities, are bounded by membership, and deny on unknown, duplicated, revoked, or cross-role subjects.
- Any usable direct slot makes access unilateral for that item and suppresses the witnessed/quorum claim; no policy replay may hide or relabel it.
- Genesis is trust-on-first-use. Every later operation is signed by an owner authorized in the immediately preceding state and binds previous/result hashes.
- Effective reader, approver, witness, quorum, access-mode, or workload changes produce explicit revisions and invalidate incompatible pending authorization.
- Principal keys are immutable. Replacement atomically carries only explicitly selected authority to a fresh same-role principal.
- PrincipalId and ItemId reuse is rejected across the complete lineage history, including replaced, revoked, deleted, and tombstoned entries.

## Required Work

- Generate a new `VaultId` through the shared J03 generator and implement owner-signed genesis and deterministic policy revision verification; caller-chosen IDs remain limited to typed import and deterministic vector paths.
- Implement vault-principal, approver, and witness lifecycle plus direct roles and witnessed item requirements.
- Implement normalized operations for membership, quorum, mode, operation, lifetime, workload, tombstone, and same-role replacement changes.
- Validate historical authority at each sequence and reject ambiguous forks or illegal combinations.
- Expose value-free capability and downgrade explanations without item-body decryption.

## Required Tests

Cover owner/direct role matrices, approver/witness membership and quorum matrices, zero/over-capacity quorum, duplicate/cross-role identities, mode transitions, direct-slot suppression, missing/reordered/forged operations, sole-owner protection, pending-request invalidation, replacement, rollback/fork fixtures, and property-model comparison. Exercise propagated vault-identifier entropy/retry failure, known source/destination lineage collision, principal and item identifier reuse anywhere in lineage history, and absence of partially signed genesis state.

## Dependencies

J03 and J05. Unblocks J07, J09, J10, J16, J20, and deferred J15.
close_reason: Completed: implemented generated owner-signed genesis, deterministic authenticated policy replay, exact normalized-state hashing, principal/item lifecycle and rotation rules, direct and witnessed access evaluation, and bounded witness policy/quorum/workload binding.

title: J07 — Implement direct/witnessed item envelopes and rekeying
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Implement format-v1 item protection for both direct and witnessed access after J19 acceptance. Witnessed-only items must not contain an implicit direct fallback.

## Why This Task Exists

Per-item, per-revision secrets bound the damage of any authorized release and prevent whole-vault or epoch material from becoming an ambient capability. Direct and witnessed access therefore converge only at the same narrowly scoped revision-secret boundary.

## Outcome

Each item revision has private names and values, separate descriptor/body secrets, fresh revision seals, algorithm-tagged direct and witnessed slots, signed ancestry, and atomic rekeying.

## Required Work

- Encrypt names and values independently and expose them only through authorized guarded access.
- Implement revision-scoped direct capsules and the exact J19-bound witnessed capsule construction.
- Bind lineage, item, epoch, revision, content role, suite, policy, and RevisionSealId into every context and authenticated datum.
- Never serialize, return, or reconstruct an epoch root or reusable witness contribution at the application boundary.
- Implement grant, revoke, rotate, principal replacement, witness-set change, and cover reseal as signed atomic mutations.
- Treat a usable direct slot as unilateral authority and suppress the item-level quorum claim.
- Preserve honest retention limits: neither mode can make an authorized endpoint forget a revision already opened.
- Generate every new `ItemId` through the shared J03 generator; caller-supplied exact bytes remain limited to typed import and deterministic vector paths.

## Required Tests

Cover both round trips; witnessed-only access; direct downgrade; cross-item/revision/role/seal swaps; stale policy; duplicate slots; partial/replayed contributions; retained revision-N endpoint state against revision N+1; rekey interruption; entropy failure; and absence of plaintext names, values, roots, or contributions from logs and public state. Exercise propagated item-identifier entropy/retry failure, collision against the full lineage followed by successful bounded regeneration, collision exhaustion, and absence of a partially published item or revision.

## Dependencies

J02, J03, J04, J05, J06, and J19. Unblocks J08, J11, J16, J17, and deferred J15.

title: J08 — Implement the mode-neutral `ItemAccessProvider`
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Freeze one guarded access boundary for both modes and deliver its direct backend. J22 must implement the witnessed backend against this same contract; callers never receive a raw key or witness-material escape hatch.

## Why This Task Exists

CLI and downstream callers must not gain a bypass merely because direct and witnessed authorization use different machinery. One narrow provider contract keeps mode, private keys, contributions, and revision secrets behind the owning boundary while giving consumers identical cleanup and failure semantics.

## Outcome

ItemAccessProvider exposes a scoped consumer operation for one authenticated descriptor/body revision, with sync core semantics and an asynchronous completion boundary suitable for witnessed requests.

## Required Work

- Validate public policy and exact slot bindings before any decapsulation or witnessed completion.
- Model direct completion plus typed witnessed pending, approved, denied, expired, stale, replay, unavailable, cancelled, and insufficient-quorum outcomes.
- Keep private identity operations inside providers.
- Pass only ProtectedRevisionSecrets to the scoped consumer and wipe intermediate direct or witnessed state on success, error, cancellation, and contained panic.
- Return stable value-free error kinds.
- Provide test doubles without production key bypasses.

## Required Tests

Cover wrong principal, role, item, epoch, policy, slot, suite, revision seal, and access mode; closure cleanup; cancellation; compile-fail raw-key/root/contribution escape; and provider failure.

## Dependencies

J22 consumes this provider contract indirectly through J10. Dependencies: J02, J04, and J07. Unblocks J10.
acceptance_criteria: CLI-facing APIs cannot request identity private keys, epoch roots, contributions, or revision secrets; each provider releases only one selected descriptor/body revision to a scoped consumer; the public interface contains no direct-only assumption; direct and witnessed backends share the same success and cleanup boundary; cleanup is observable through test instrumentation.

title: J09 — Implement per-principal audit, checkpoints, and local receipts
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

This task covers principal-local audit and authenticated checkpoints for both access modes. J23 owns offline witness-decision receipts and server operations; both are mandatory release work.

## Why This Task Exists

A vault-wide audit key would require unrelated authority to be unlocked and would turn local verification into another shared secret. Principal-local roots and monotonic checkpoints detect tamper and rollback without putting private evidence into the portable Git artifact.

## Outcome

Each principal can verify its own append-only local audit trail and detect rollback relative to retained authenticated checkpoints without placing local custody state in the portable vault.

## Required Work

- Define signed or MACed, bounded audit entries for direct and witnessed access, request/decision state changes, and mutations.
- Link witnessed entries to bounded request, decision, receipt, policy-revision, and revision-seal identifiers without recording private names, values, manifests, contributions, or reusable authorization material.
- Store checkpoints and audit state outside .jury/vault.json under a disjoint local state root.
- Make rollback and truncation detectable relative to retained local state and report the limits for fresh clones or lost state.
- Keep paths, secrets, values, private keys, and decrypted payloads out of audit data and errors.

## Required Tests

Cover append, checkpoint, verification, truncation, reordering, substitution, rollback with and without retained state, crash boundaries, concurrent access, fresh clones, corrupted local state, and secret-leak scans.

## Dependencies

J04, J05, and J06. Unblocks J10, J16, and J17; it also supports post-0.x J15 compatibility.

## Legacy Baseline and Provenance

Use https://github.com/bpcakes/jig-sh.git at exact commit eed70cee337b0067ed92deb9fa05017b0b284605; a sibling ../jig-sh is only an object source after the commit and every selected path verifies. If the exact object or a named path is unavailable, this task blocks rather than substituting another revision, build output, or the preserved source-plan snapshot.

Inspect:

- crates/jig-vault/src/audit.rs;
- audit append/read primitives in crates/jig-vault/src/store.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/management.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/lifecycle.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/exec.rs.

Port tamper, forged insertion, blank-line, torn-tail, missing-log, append-failure, and value-leakage cases. Replace the v2 DEK-derived audit key, global audit identity, and whole-vault unlock assumptions with principal-local roots, checkpoints, and value-free events.

title: J10 — Deliver witnessed-aware partial-unlock sessions and scoped snapshots
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Session state must support witnessed open before the CLI freezes. Opening a vault never means decrypting all bodies, and a pending or failed witness request never becomes direct access.

## Why This Task Exists

Session scope is the secret-lifetime boundary visible to product surfaces. It must release only the selected descriptor or body, keep inaccessible names out of memory, and apply the same cancellation and cleanup rules whether authority is direct or witnessed.

## Outcome

A principal sees only authorized descriptor metadata and opens an item body only after explicit direct authorization or completion of a witnessed request for the exact operation and revision seal.

## Required Work

- Model locked, public-validated, principal, witness-pending, approved, denied, expired, stale, replay, unavailable, cancelled, failed, and unlocked-item states.
- Hold only scoped protected capabilities and accessible value-free metadata.
- Bind transitions to the exact request, action manifest, revision token, policy checkpoint, witness set, session, and expiry.
- Integrate ItemAccessProvider rather than identity or witness keys.
- Enforce inactivity, absolute expiry, cancellation, signal, refresh-failure, and error cleanup.
- Keep values, keys, epoch roots, and contributions behind guarded operations and out of snapshots.

## Required Tests

Cover partial authorization, ordinary-open/body-decryption counters, full witnessed transition matrix, approval broadening, refresh and expiry races, response substitution, insufficient quorum, cancellation, inaccessible-name absence, concurrent use, and wipe-on-lock/exit.

J06, J08, J09, and J19. Unblocks J11, J13, J14, J15, J16, J17, J22, and J24.

title: J14 — Deliver transparent exec and brokered run
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Deliver the mode-neutral process channel used by direct and witnessed operations. J22 binds witnessed authorization and the exact action manifest before this layer may spawn.

## Why This Task Exists

Starting a child is an irreversible plaintext-release event. Jury must resolve and authorize every reference before spawn, deliver only the approved values, and own the complete descendant process tree so timeout, cancellation, signal, and output failures cannot leave secrets or processes behind.

## Outcome

Authorized values reach child processes through explicit, bounded channels without entering arguments, the ambient environment, logs, or persistent plaintext files.

## Required Work

- Define a mode-neutral execution contract for environment injection, stdin, file descriptors, and brokered access.
- Require an exact authorized capability from ItemAccessProvider before spawn; witness-pending, denied, expired, stale, unavailable, or insufficient-quorum states cannot spawn.
- Validate variable names, executable resolution, working directories, output sinks, and placeholder mapping.
- Contain and terminate process trees on cancellation, timeout, signal, and parent failure.
- Restore terminal state and wipe protected buffers on every exit path.
- Clearly report platform limitations and unsupported containment modes.

## Required Tests

Cover hostile variable names and paths, child/grandchild cleanup, cancellation and signal races, output capture bounds, inherited descriptor leaks, core-dump settings, terminal restoration, and scans of process listings, logs, and temporary storage.

## Dependencies

J10, J12, and J13. Unblocks J22 and J25.

## Legacy Baseline and Provenance

Use https://github.com/bpcakes/jig-sh.git at exact commit eed70cee337b0067ed92deb9fa05017b0b284605; a sibling ../jig-sh is only an object source after the commit and every selected path verifies. Reuse all-or-nothing resolution, no-child-on-failure, environment stripping, streaming redaction, timeout, signal, exact-status, output-cap, and process-tree failure cases. Replace v2 unlocking, Jig reference types, and Jig-owned plaintext delivery.

title: J19A — Select the witnessed construction and freeze its threat model
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

This outcome is mandatory for the experimental witnessed-access 0.x release. It remains pre-alpha, must not be used for real secrets, and may claim only properties proved under the accepted construction and deployment assumptions.

## Project Boundary

Jury is a standalone Linux CLI plus self-hostable witness service using jury-vault format v1 and witness protocol v1. It must not depend on Jig at runtime, expose private keys, epoch roots, reusable contributions, or plaintext through adapters, or use non-generic fixtures. Direct slots remain explicitly unilateral and outside every quorum claim.

## Why This Task Exists

The endpoint-retention promise is a property of a complete construction and its
compromise model, not of “using multiple witnesses.” Selecting the construction
before schemas or provider adapters prevents availability, coordination, or a
static share-release shortcut from being mislabeled distributed authority.

## Outcome

`docs/security/witness-v1/construction.md` and
`docs/security/witness-v1/threat-model.md` select one implementable construction
and freeze its exact trust boundaries, compromise assumptions, availability and
revocation limits, direct-slot interaction, and falsifiable endpoint-retention
claim.

## Required Work

- compare maintained threshold-KEM, distributed-decryption, and other publicly
  specified candidates with applicable public analysis against the exact J01B primitive/provider evidence and J03
  domain semantics; record every rejected candidate and concrete rejection
  reason;
- specify approver, witness, endpoint, `juryd`, storage, clock, network, and
  external-anchor trust boundaries;
- state quorum, collusion, malicious-client, compromised-approver,
  compromised-witness, offline-witness, rollback, replay, expiry, restored-state,
  rotation, and recovery assumptions;
- decide whether construction-internal epoch material exists and prove that no
  conforming endpoint reconstructs or receives an epoch root or reusable
  contribution;
- define exactly what a previously authorized endpoint may retain and why that
  state can reopen only its already released revision, not a later
  `RevisionSealId` without a fresh authorized quorum;
- state direct and mixed-slot semantics: any usable direct slot is unilateral,
  defeats the item-level quorum claim, and is never an implicit fallback;
- pin the exact construction and provider-binding inputs that J19B, J19C, and J19
  must use, while retaining the pre-alpha/no-real-secrets boundary.

## Required Verification

- actor/compromise and quorum matrices cover every stated threshold and excluded
  compromise case;
- a retained-state inventory covers long-term endpoint keys, all prior requests,
  approvals, responses, contributions, revision secrets, ciphertexts, and
  plaintext;
- each claimed property maps to a construction assumption or remains an explicit
  nonclaim;
- alternative comparison uses current primary specifications and exact provider
  behavior rather than names or popularity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- one construction and provider binding are selected with no unresolved design
  alternatives;
- endpoint-retention and revision-freshness claims are explicit, falsifiable, and
  bounded by named assumptions;
- trust, compromise, revocation, rollback, replay, rotation, recovery, and
  availability limits are complete;
- no static share-release or coordination-only shortcut survives;
- direct access is explicitly unilateral and outside the witnessed claim.

## Dependencies

J01B and J03.

## Unblocks

J19B.

## Live Tracker Dependencies

- J01B: `jury-qv4.1.2`
- J03: `jury-qv4.2.2`

Unblocks J19B: `jury-qv4.4.7`.
close_reason: Completed: selected revision-scoped Shamir shares sealed with the J01B X-Wing HPKE suite; construction, provider binding, retention claim, compromise matrix, and recovery limits are frozen.

title: J19B — Freeze witnessed protocol schemas and authorization state machines
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

This outcome is mandatory for the experimental witnessed-access 0.x release. It remains pre-alpha, must not be used for real secrets, and may claim only properties proved under the accepted construction and deployment assumptions.

## Project Boundary

Jury is a standalone Linux CLI plus self-hostable witness service using jury-vault format v1 and witness protocol v1. It must not depend on Jig at runtime, expose private keys, epoch roots, reusable contributions, or plaintext through adapters, or use non-generic fixtures. Direct slots remain explicitly unilateral and outside every quorum claim.

## Why This Task Exists

Individually valid signatures do not make a semantically consistent request.
The protocol must freeze one canonical meaning and one crash-safe authorization
state machine before vectors, servers, or clients can implement it differently.

## Outcome

`docs/security/witness-v1/protocol.md` and
`docs/security/witness-v1/state-machines.md` freeze canonical protocol-v1
schemas, preimages, meaningful approval rules, and deterministic request,
approval, contribution, replay, expiry, cancellation, checkpoint, anchor,
rotation, and recovery transitions for the J19A construction.

## Required Work

- define bounded canonical encodings and domain-separated preimages for requests,
  action manifests, approver descriptors and decisions, witness contributions,
  decisions, receipts, checkpoints, anchors, rotation, and recovery records;
- bind vault, genesis, item, epoch, content role, revision,
  `RevisionSealId`, policy, requester, operation, workload, expiry, nonce,
  request-specific session key, witness set, and protocol suite;
- specify `ApprovalTargetV1`, owner-signed non-secret review labels,
  entitlement-bound private-name display, field/working-directory/output-sink
  openings, label rotation, and fail-closed human approval whenever a complete
  verified meaningful representation is unavailable;
- define one common request/action-manifest validator that rejects every
  semantically inconsistent pair before display, automatic approval, approval
  signing, policy matching, or witness counting;
- define independent approver and witness membership, both quorums, duplicate
  and substitution rejection, replay, skew, not-before, expiry, cancellation,
  concurrency, key rotation, and direct-downgrade behavior;
- define first registration, strict-descendant checkpoint advancement,
  witness-behind/stale/fork outcomes, revocation propagation, restored-witness
  recovery, and the exact limit of witnessed freshness;
- define a public self-hostable external rollback-anchor interface;
- freeze database commit, signed next-candidate creation, external
  compare-and-swap, exact readback, response release, and crash reconciliation;
  only one exact signed pending candidate may reconcile, and every other
  database/anchor disagreement fails closed;
- define bounded value-free rejection codes; unknown versions, implicit direct
  downgrade, opaque-only human approval, and transport-authentication-as-consent
  fail closed.

## Required Verification

- transition tables cover replay, expiry, cancellation, concurrent identical and
  conflicting requests, rotation, restore, rollback, anchor loss/conflict, and
  the sole safe pending-candidate recovery;
- every duplicated request/manifest field has an individually valid mismatch
  case rejected before display or counting;
- complete meaningful rendering and opaque-target refusal are specified at every
  supported presentation boundary;
- no accepted state or message releases an epoch root or reusable contribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- every accepted message has one canonical encoding and one domain-separated
  signature or contribution preimage;
- request/manifest mismatch fails before display, approval, policy evaluation,
  or contribution assembly;
- approval requires a complete policy-authenticated meaningful target, not only
  a digest, opaque selector, or unauthenticated label;
- replay, expiry, cancellation, concurrency, rotation, restore, rollback, and
  split-write transitions are deterministic;
- unknown versions, transport-only consent, and implicit direct downgrade fail
  closed.

## Dependencies

J19A.

## Unblocks

J19C; deferred optional J19R.

## Live Tracker Dependencies

- J19A: jury-qv4.4.6

Unblocks J19C: jury-qv4.4.8.
Unblocks deferred optional J19R: jury-qv4.4.10.

title: J25 — Complete the witnessed adversarial corpus and measured budgets
description: Join the active security boundaries with cross-boundary end-to-end adversarial cases, fuzz/property targets, failure injection, leak scans, and measured resource budgets; owning tasks retain ordinary negative/crash tests. Cover Git as untrusted transport, strict-descendant import and divergence refusal, direct/witnessed flows, witness recovery, processes, and capacity refusal. Run a bounded named repository-leak scan and enumerate inspected surfaces; never call it universal proof. Measure portable KDF/protected-memory and lifecycle behavior on Linux. Exclude TUI, hardware protectors, managed service, semantic merge, Jig migration, rollover, and suite migration. Dependencies: J11, J14, J16, J17, J20, J21, J22, and J23.
acceptance_criteria: Every public parser and durable transaction has its owning test evidence; active cross-boundary cases pass in native Linux CI; strict-descendant and divergence behavior is covered; provider and misuse/resource oracles match J01A; measurements make no guessed SLO claim; unresolved medium-or-higher security findings block J26; scoped leak evidence is never presented as universal proof.

title: J26 — Publish the experimental witnessed-access 0.x release
description: Publish one exact externally-unreviewed pre-alpha witnessed-access candidate with a native Linux binary, checksums, SBOM, provenance, reproducible build instructions, current dependency/advisory review, signing-key procedures, incident/security reporting, and exact J19/source/build binding. Dogfood generic direct and witnessed-only CLI lifecycles, self-hosted juryd, strict-descendant import, divergence refusal, backup drill/restore, and witnessed recovery on Linux. Do not ship or advertise macOS, Windows, TUI, hardware identity protectors, managed topology, semantic merge, Jig migration, rollover, suite migration, or external review. Dependencies: J22, J23, and J25.
acceptance_criteria: All active leaves are complete; direct/witnessed conformance and adversarial suites pass; the native Linux artifact completes the generic lifecycle and no macOS or Windows artifact is published; exact source/verifier/provider/build/artifact binding invalidates on change; no unresolved medium-or-higher finding remains; deferred surfaces are absent; every release surface states externally unreviewed pre-alpha and unsuitable for real secrets.
